It’s more like sudden, graphic images of something bad happening to my husband or my kids, or this impulse like, “What if I just swerved the car into oncoming traffic?” I don’t want these thoughts at all—they feel foreign and disgusting—but they pop up over and over.

When they hit, I completely lose my train of thought. My mind just blanks out, like someone wiped a whiteboard clean. I’ll be staring at the computer screen and can’t remember what I was doing. It happens at work, at home, even when I’m trying to relax and watch TV with my husband.

I spend a lot of time mentally fighting these thoughts, trying to push them away, but the more I try not to think them, the more they intrude. It’s exhausting and makes it hard to concentrate on my job or enjoy anything.
